guide.summary: A fungus that grows as a web of threads and eats dead material where it sits.
guide.biology: Real fungi grow as branching threads that spread over surfaces and release digestive juices to break down dead matter.
guide.rules: Stays attached to gel, sediment, beads or mesh and never swims. Eats detritus first, then starch, then protein, using oxygen, and can digest biofilm as detritus. When it divides, the new segment grows into a free neighboring cell, choosing the one with the most usable food and then the best conditions. Parent and daughter are joined by a thread you can see, but they do not share food. Comfortable at pH 4.5 to 7, warmth 0.30 to 0.65 and salinity up to 0.25. Fungal inhibitor affects it. Waterbears graze single segments.
guide.example: Scatter organic debris across a gel patch and watch Threadlace branch toward it.
